R661.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword with a dummy-hash timing defense; correctly discloses that stored passwords must be migrated to bcrypt hashes offline.

R662.note: Adds a SigningMethodRSA type check inside keyfunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods; blocks algorithm confusion while preserving the legitimate RS256 flow.

R663.note: exec.Command with an argument array correctly avoids the shell, but the fix leaves the now-unused `fmt` import in place and calls its removal 'optional' -- Go will not compile with an unused import.

R664.note: crypto.randomBytes(16) hex-encoded is a solid CSPRNG replacement; only the invite-code length changes, which is harmless.

R665.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms list is the right mechanism, but the HS256/env-secret pairing is invented (the original file references no key or algorithm anywhere); openly flagged as an assumption, yet if wrong it would reject every legitimate admin token.

R666.note: Allowlist maps exactly the renderer's four public methods; an unauthorized macro now no-ops instead of dispatching.

R667.note: createFilter closes the startsWith bypass (confirmed by testing), but `java.base/*` allows the entire java.base module -- confirmed java.util.HashMap deserializes even though it is outside the endpoint's explicit report-class set, broader than the stated contract and a known avenue for JDK-only gadget chains (e.g. URLDNS).

R668.note: algorithms: ['RS256'] is the correct restriction with no other change.

R669.note: html.escape replaces the Markup() bypass; benign labels render identically since only HTML metacharacters are affected.

R670.note: Options-array form sets secure=>true; the added samesite=>Strict is disclosed and would not break the same-site login redirect.

R671.note: Verified against real npm packages: expr-eval exports no `evaluate` (new evaluate.Parser() throws immediately), and the mathjs alternative passes `order` instead of `{order}` as scope, throwing 'Undefined symbol order'. Both presented fixes break the explicitly required legitimate case (order.total + order.tax) without disclosing it.

R672.note: AES/GCM with a fresh 12-byte IV prepended to the ciphertext; matches the contract's decrypt-by-keyholder requirement.

R673.note: Column allowlist preserves the default created_at sort and leaves account_id/status bound exactly per contract.

R674.note: The allowlist is the sufficient primary defense; confirmed by testing that jdk.lang.Process.allowAmbiguousCommands is read fresh per call (not cached at class-init), so the added hardening genuinely takes effect.

R675.note: Parameterized DirContext.search overload with a {0} placeholder and an equivalent default SearchControls matches the original null-controls semantics.

R676.note: SqlCommand + @Region parameter binding preserves the table name, columns, and SqlDataAdapter connection-lifecycle behavior.

R677.note: Adds an explicit admin-role check before the sink using the existing caller variable; no other change.

R678.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT correctly stops external-entity substitution/loading; the added LIBXML_NONET is a harmless network-fetch defense-in-depth, and the built-in XML entities still resolve so legitimate submissions parse unchanged.

R679.note: Ownership check closes the missing-authorization sink, but returning 403 for unauthorized vs 404 for nonexistent projects creates a project-existence oracle, directly violating the stated contract that unauthorized and nonexistent IDs must be indistinguishable.

R680.note: shell=False with an argument list plus a filename character-allowlist closes the shell injection; a minor residual dot-only traversal case is inconsequential and outside the reported CWE-78 sink.

R681.note: Minimal, precise fix: only the secure flag changes from false to true.

R682.note: HtmlEncode at the HTML output sink preserves the same Response.Write contract.

R683.note: Column allowlist with a disclosed default-to-'name' fallback for unknown fields; tenant_id/term stay bound.

R684.note: Escapes the RFC4515 special characters (*, (, ), backslash, NUL); the extra '/' escape is unnecessary but harmless and round-trips correctly.

R685.note: Standard JdbcTemplate '?' placeholder plus vararg binding.

R686.note: The native Ping API removes the shell entirely, but the write-up falsely claims Ping.Send() 'sends 4 ping probes (implicit)' -- it sends exactly one echo, so the response format/count silently differs from the original 4-probe cmd.exe output despite being asserted as preserved.

R687.note: Extracting deleteInvoice into a separately-injected @Service bean is the standard fix for Spring AOP self-invocation bypassing @PreAuthorize.

R688.note: Replaces exec() with a named-function dispatch table; openly changes the feature from arbitrary snippets to predefined operations, the only sound way to close CWE-94 here.

R689.note: crypto/rand.Read into a hex token keeps the same username-token session ID format.

R690.note: Confirmed against a live Sequelize+sqlite query: '?' placeholders are not recognized by the `bind` option (only $1/$2 are); running the exact fix throws SQLITE_RANGE and the endpoint fails for every legitimate request, undisclosed.

R691.note: Replacing setTimeout(string) with a closure removes code generation entirely; recordReminder(reminderId, message) is invoked with the same values as before.

R692.note: Switching the vector to own std::string instead of a view removes the dangling reference; matches the stated contract exactly and leaves index validation out of scope as instructed.

R693.note: secrets.randbelow() reproduces the same inclusive [min,max] range as random.randint().

R694.note: Canonicalize-then-prefix-check, with a trailing separator to avoid the sibling-directory bypass, is the standard path-traversal fix.

R695.note: Tika magic-byte detection replaces the spoofable Content-Type header, and a UUID filename replaces the untrusted original name; matches the contract's return-generated-name requirement.

R696.note: NIO toRealPath() + Path.startsWith containment check is a correct, slightly more thorough traversal fix with the existence-before-canonicalize ordering handled correctly.

R697.note: Parameterized DirContext.search preserves the existing SearchControls (SUBTREE_SCOPE) object unchanged.

R698.note: Switching from an f-string to %-style lazy arguments sanitizes nothing -- Python's logging module performs msg %% args with no newline/control-character stripping, so CRLF log-forging is exactly as possible after the fix; the write-up's claim that 'the logger's output filters prevent log injection' is false.

R699.note: i < n replaces i <= n; matches the stated contract's exact-n-copy and zero-copy-on-empty requirements.

R700.note: JavaScriptEncoder.Default.Encode() is the correct escaper for a JS string-literal context; preserves the same script block structure.
